ratings.reviewer_notes: Review-level discussion stating that metformin blocks the LKB1/AMPK/mTOR/S6K1 growth pathway in glioblastoma stem cells; no primary mechanistic experiment is described.
Shows metformin increases phospho-AMPK in HeLa cells through reduced AMPK O-GlcNAcylation, but does not assess mTOR signaling.
In colorectal cancer cells, metformin activated AMPK and suppressed the mTOR pathway and its S6 and 4EBP1 downstream targets, alongside reduced proliferation.

Direct mechanistic evidence in gastric cancer cells: AMPK knockdown and forced expression of the mTOR effector p70S6K1 attenuated metformin-induced survivin inhibition and apoptosis; xenografts supported the pathway.
Metformin activated AMPK and reduced phosphorylation of mTOR, p70S6K, and 4E-BP1 in HeLa cancer cells, with cell-line-specific effects linked to LKB1 status.
Tests OSU-53 rather than metformin, but provides an informative cancer-cell model of AMPK activation with mTOR suppression; metformin is mentioned only as a related AMPK-activating agent.
Studies engineered CAR T cells rather than cancer cells and concludes that metformin's AMPK-dependent functional effects are mTOR/HIF1alpha-independent.
Directly evaluates metformin in liver cancer cells but finds mTORC1 inhibition occurs through AMPK-independent REDD1, providing relevant evidence for an alternative mechanism.
In MCF-7 breast cancer cells, metformin increased phospho-AMPK and decreased phosphorylation of the mTOR downstream target p70S6K; antiproliferative effects were described as AMPK-mediated.

Metformin plus pitavastatin activated AMPK and inhibited PI3K/mTOR signaling in pancreatic cancer cells, but the combination design does not establish metformin-specific AMPK-mediated mTOR inhibition.
Metformin altered genes associated with AMPK and mTOR pathways in HeLa cells, but pathway activity and an AMPK-to-mTOR causal link were not directly demonstrated.

Strong direct evidence in myeloma: metformin activated AMPK, induced TSC2 phosphorylation, repressed mTORC1/2 and downstream 4EBP1/AKT signaling, and inhibited growth in an AMPK-dependent manner in vitro and in xenografts.

Shows that 6PGD inhibition or physcion activates AMPK and suppresses mTOR in esophageal cancer, with metformin used in an effective combination; metformin-specific pathway mediation is not clearly tested.
Direct breast cancer-cell study stating that metformin inhibits mTOR through AMPK signaling and using AMPK siRNA to support AMPK-dependent effects on IRS-1 and AKT.
In human esophageal cancer cells and a rat carcinogenesis model, metformin activated AMPK while reducing p-mTOR, p-p70S6K, and cyclin D1, alongside antiproliferative and proapoptotic effects.
Review summarizing evidence that metformin-induced AMPK and REDD1 activation can inhibit mTOR in cancer cells, while also discussing alternative bioenergetic and antifolate mechanisms.
Broad review of metformin in malignancies affecting women that identifies AMPK/mTOR as one of several proposed antitumor pathways.

Demonstrates AMPK-dependent metformin-induced apoptosis and UPR inhibition in ALL cells; rapamycin implicates mTOR-regulated protein synthesis, but metformin-mediated mTOR inhibition is not directly shown.
A review specifically focused on the role of AMPK/mTOR signaling in metformin's anticancer activity, providing synthesis rather than new primary evidence.
Direct evidence in bile duct cancer cells: metformin phosphorylated AMPK at Thr172, activated TSC2, and inhibited mTOR; hyperglycemia impaired these effects.

The metformin–PP242 combination activated AMPK and blocked mTORC1/2 in colorectal cancer cells, but direct mTOR inhibition by PP242 confounds attribution of mTOR suppression to metformin-mediated AMPK activation.
Epidemiologic cohort associating metformin use with reduced cancer incidence; it contains no cancer-cell or AMPK/mTOR mechanistic evidence.
